summary: Today’s pulse tracks Ukraine confirms strikes on oil refinery in Russia’s Tatarstan – Europe live, Max Miller to stay on Ohio ballots despite pressure to drop out of race after domestic abuse allegations – live, and Amber heat-health alerts issued for most of England as temperatures could reach 36C or higher this week – latest updates. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are health, would, and early. In the background, Amnesty International says Farage putting ‘hate and inhumanity’ before leadership with El Salvador prison plan– UK politics live and People flocking to Spain to view solar eclipse could spark more ‘devastating’ wildfires keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Ukraine confirms strikes on oil refinery in Russia’s Tatarstan – Europe live
headlines.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that strikes on such facilities were directly linked with putting more pressure on Moscow A fire ⁠broke ⁠out ​at an ⁠industrial facility in ⁠Russia’s ​Tyumen ‌region ‌in Siberia ‌after several drones fell on it, ‌ Tyumen region ​governor Alexander Moor ⁠said ​on his Telegram ​channel. This is reported by Reuters.

headlines.title: Max Miller to stay on Ohio ballots despite pressure to drop out of race after domestic abuse allegations – live
headlines.description: The House Republican has been disavowed by his own party amid allegations that he has been abusive toward his ex-wife and daughter This comes after the death of long-serving Senator Lindsey Graham last month. Graham had won the Republican nomination for the Senate seat he had held for 23 years. His sister, Darline Graham , was appointed to finish the final months of his term and is running to take his place as the GOP nominee. She’s also received Trump’s endorsement.

headlines.title: Amber heat-health alerts issued for most of England as temperatures could reach 36C or higher this week – latest updates
headlines.description: The upgraded alerts will be in place from 9am on Tuesday until 9pm on Friday An 18-year-old died after getting into difficulty in the sea at Camber Sands beach, East Sussex, yesterday, bringing the number of deaths in open-water incidents over the hot, dry summer to over 40, according to estimates compiled by the Press Association. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has updated heat-health alerts for nine regions in England, warning that rising temperatures this week may increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups. It’s important that everyone is aware of the simple steps they can take to stay safe during periods of hot weather. Drinking plenty of water, avoiding the sun during the hottest part of the day and keeping indoor spaces cool are all things you can do to keep yourself and others safe. For vulnerable groups including older adults and those with existing health conditions, warmer weather than result in serious health outcomes.

headlines.title: Amnesty International says Farage putting ‘hate and inhumanity’ before leadership with El Salvador prison plan– UK politics live
headlines.description: A spokesperson for the human rights group likened the proposal to ‘financial brutality with British taxpayers’ money’ Farage and Yusuf are now taking questions. Q: [From Jack Fenwick from the BBC] Are there other countries where you might send foreign offenders? And how much would this cost? We have to admit that there might not be too many colour TVs. It’s not going to be a summer camp. It’s not going to be particularly fun. But it won’t be cruel and it won’t be unreasonable. We will rapidly build capacity. We will take advantage of new prefabricated modular technology and build 12,000 prison places in the form of Nightingale prisons on Ministry of Defence land. And the army will be called in to assist. Together, these measures will create an additional 22,000 prison places compared to Andy Burnham’s plans.

headlines.title: People flocking to Spain to view solar eclipse could spark more ‘devastating’ wildfires
headlines.description: Northern Spain will be one of the best places in world to view phenomenon with 460,000 extra visitors expected Authorities in Spain have warned of an increased risk of fires when hundreds of thousands of people head to the hills and beaches to get a better view of Wednesday’s total solar eclipse . “The vegetation is extraordinarily dry and the smallest spark or carelessness could lead to devastating forest fires,” the environment minister, Sara Aagesen, said on a visit to Niebla in the south of the country, the site of Spain’s latest fire.

headlines.title: PM urged not to change scheme to stop PC Andrew Harper killers’ early release
headlines.description: Manslaughter exemption would mean more releases would be needed within 18 months, Prison Service officials say What could Andy Burnham do to block early release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers? Andy Burnham has been warned that changing the terms of the prisoners’ early release scheme so PC Andrew Harper’s killers are kept behind bars would force another spate of early releases before the next general election. Prison Service officials have told No 10 that adding an exemption so that those convicted of manslaughter, such as Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, remain in jail would mean further early releases would be needed within 18 months.

headlinePool.title: John Lewis managing director Peter Ruis quits job after less than three years
headlinePool.description: Surprise departure comes after department store chain’s chair warned of ‘really tough trading conditions’ Business live – latest updates The managing director of John Lewis has quit the job after less than three years in charge of the British department store chain, as the company faces “really tough” trading conditions. Peter Ruis will leave the business in order to “pursue new projects”, John Lewis said in a statement on Monday.

headlinePool.title: Louisiana warns beachgoers amid surge in flesh-eating bacteria infections
headlinePool.description: State confirms nine cases, including five deaths, from Vibrio vulnificus organism, which thrives in seawater Health officials in Louisiana are urging beachgoers to take precautions during a summertime surge in infections from a flesh-eating bacteria found in coastal waters. Louisiana has confirmed nine cases of Vibrio vulnificus infections this year, the state’s health department said last week in a news release. All were hospitalized, and five died. During the same period over the previous decade, Louisiana reported an average of seven cases and one death.

headlinePool.title: At least 13 killed in Ukrainian drone strike deep into Russia
headlinePool.description: Russian officials say another 75 people were injured by the attack in the Tatarstan region, one of the deadliest Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia since Moscow's full-scale invasion.

headlinePool.title: Crew of Zuckerberg yacht did not hear radio call to assist boat, Meta says
headlinePool.description: Small skiff ran out of fuel off Alaska and was helped by cruise ship even though Meta CEO’s vessel was closer Zuckerberg faces questions over why superyacht reportedly declined to help stranded boat The crew of a yacht owned by Mark Zuckerberg did not hear a radio call for a maritime assist from a small skiff that ran out of fuel off the coast of Alaska, and by the time it did, another nearby ship had already rendered assistance, a spokesperson for the Meta CEO said. The Alaska Beacon news outlet reported that the skiff had issued a call for assistance through the US Coast Guard last week and a nearby small cruise ship, the Wilderness Legacy, towed it into nearby Farragut Bay in south-east Alaska and refueled it.

headlinePool.title: Drought expected to be declared in more parts of England ahead of possible 36C heat
headlinePool.description: North-west could join other parts of country in drought, and amber heat health alerts issued for much of England Drought is expected to be declared in more areas of England as the UK braces for its fifth heatwave of the summer. The National Drought Group, whose members include the government, water companies, the National Farmers’ Union, the Met Office and conservation experts, will meet on Monday to assess the situation across England.

headlinePool.title: Flood death toll in India's Assam reaches 100 as thousands lose their homes
headlinePool.description: Days of heavy monsoon rain has caused rivers, including the Brahmaputra, to overflow, inundating communities, disrupting livelihoods and damaging infrastructure.

headlinePool.title: Battle for Mali base has killed dozens of militants, army says
headlinePool.description: The army says it was involved in fierce fighting but disputes that Islamists took control of the garrison.

headlinePool.title: Alleged rebel leader killed in Colombia as president targets armed groups
headlinePool.description: The military operation against Hernando Forero Mosquera was carried out just days after Colombia's new president was sworn in.

headlinePool.title: Decades of abuse revealed at Michigan art school. And, the Iran war's impact on midterms
headlinePool.description: A new report has revealed decades of alleged abuse at an elite art school. NPR spoke with one of the victims. And, Iran is playing the long game with negotiations, which could impact midterms.
